plan: Replace the Triton SwiGLU with a minimal hand-bound C++/CUDA extension to cut dispatcher/kernel overhead below vendor torch.compile fusion. Exactly one kernel per direction. Python layer: validate metadata and raise NotImplementedError for CPU/FP32/odd-last-dim/noncontiguous inputs, load the controller-built module kda_swiglu_stage29_002 from /tmp/kda-swiglu-stage29/cpp-build-002 via importlib spec_from_file_location (sole file access, no build/write), wrap a torch.autograd.Function that saves only x on forward and canonicalizes a possibly-noncontiguous grad with .contiguous() before backward, returning a single input gradient. C++ (pybind11) forward(x)/backward(x,grad): CUDAGuard on x.device(), current CUDA stream, TORCH_CHECK metadata, allocate output x.shape[:-1]+(H,) and dx like x, skip launch on empty, dispatch to .cu launchers. CUDA: one thread per output element i, row=i/H col=i%H gateidx=row*2H+col upidx=gateidx+H; load gate/up as FP32 via static_cast<float>(at::BFloat16), sig=1/(1+expf(-a)) (true expf, no fastmath/intrinsic/approx exp), forward stores BF16(a*sig*b); backward computes dx_gate=BF16(g*sig*(1+a*(1-sig))*b) and dx_up=BF16(g*(a*sig)), rounding only on the final stores. Indexing works for odd H; last dim must be even. Controller builds, then runs the 22-case native-compiled numerical verification (atol 3e-4/rtol 1e-3 CPU float64) and the 120-step x3-seed performance gate.
risks: 1) This is a hypothesis: a thin extension may not beat vendor torch.compile fusion on BI-V150; the perf gate (all 3 seeds >1% faster) may fail and the candidate must be preserved as failed evidence. 2) FP contraction (fma) on 1+a*(1-sig) could perturb bit-order vs native; tolerance is loose so it should pass, but if bitwise order matters the controller must record/disable contraction flags. 3) at::BFloat16 host/device conversion and data_ptr casts are assumed CoreX-supported as in prior extensions; if not, build/verify fails. 4) The .so filename is assumed <module>.so under the build dir; if the controller names it differently the importlib path must be adjusted. 5) expf must be the accurate float exp (not __expf); any fastmath build flag would break the no-approx-exp contract. 6) Two separate BF16 stores to dx per thread (gate/up) are each independent output addresses, so no write races.
